name: Ridge Regression
learningObjectives: Understand L2 regularization and how it prevents overfitting
Learn how the alpha parameter controls regularization strength
Recognize when to use Ridge regression over standard linear regression
Interpret the effect of regularization on model coefficients
Apply Ridge regression to high-dimensional data

controls.label: Dataset
controls.tooltip: Choose a dataset to train on

controls.label: Alpha (Regularization Strength)
controls.tooltip: Controls regularization strength. Higher values shrink coefficients more, preventing overfitting.

controls.label: Learning Rate
controls.tooltip: Controls how quickly the model learns.

visualizations.title: Data & Ridge Regression Line
visualizations.description: Scatter plot showing the data points and the fitted regression line with L2 regularization

visualizations.title: Training Loss
visualizations.description: Line chart showing how the loss decreases during training

visualizations.title: Weight Magnitudes
visualizations.description: Bar chart showing the magnitude of each coefficient

metrics.name: Mean Squared Error
metrics.description: Average squared difference between predictions and actual values

metrics.name: Root Mean Squared Error
metrics.description: Square root of MSE, in the same units as the target

metrics.name: R² Score
metrics.description: Proportion of variance explained by the model (1.0 is perfect)

metrics.name: Mean Absolute Error
metrics.description: Average absolute difference between predictions and actual values

metrics.name: L2 Norm of Weights
metrics.description: Magnitude of the weight vector (regularization penalty)
